 Rain Ready Sonoma: Understanding Weather & Storm Alerts
 November 13, 2026 
 By stracy@sonomacity.org 
-->
 Posted on November 13, 2026
 Sonoma received some welcome rain today, giving us our first real taste of the rainy season and a good opportunity to think about what the coming winter months may bring.
 The first significant rainfall of the season can also reveal things we may not have noticed during the dry months: gutters that aren’t draining properly, water collecting in unexpected places, slippery roads, or windshield wipers that need replacing.
 It’s a good time to take note of those little things and address them before the next storm.
 It’s also a good time to get familiar with the weather information we’ll be hearing more about in the months ahead. What’s the difference between a Flood Watch and a Flood Warning ? What does a Wind Advisory mean? And when should you take action?
 Understanding these terms can help you make informed decisions as conditions change.
 Outlooks, Watches, Advisories & Warnings: What’s the Difference?
 The National Weather Service (NWS) issues forecasts and alerts to help people understand potential weather hazards. Different terms communicate different levels of concern and urgency.
 Outlook: Something to Keep an Eye On
 An outlook provides an early indication that hazardous weather may develop in the coming days.
 It’s a heads-up to stay informed, review your plans and check for forecast updates. The details may change as the event gets closer.
 Watch: Be Prepared
 A watch means conditions are favorable for a particular weather hazard, but the event is not certain.
 For example, a Flood Watch means flooding is possible within the designated area.
 This is the time to pay closer attention to forecasts and consider whether you need to take additional precautions, particularly if your home, business or regular travel routes have experienced flooding before.
 Advisory: Use Caution
 An advisory is issued when weather conditions are expected to cause inconvenience or potentially hazardous situations that warrant caution.
 For example, a Wind Advisory may be issued when gusty winds could make driving difficult, especially for high-profile vehicles, or cause unsecured objects to blow around.
 Advisories shouldn’t be ignored. Even conditions that don’t meet warning criteria can cause local disruptions.
 Warning: Take Action
 A warning means hazardous weather is occurring, imminent or expected, and conditions may pose a significant threat to life or property.
 A Flood Warning , for example, means flooding is occurring or expected in the warned area.
 Follow official instructions, avoid hazardous areas and take appropriate protective action.
 Remember: A watch means prepare. A warning means act. 
 View current weather forecasts, watches, advisories and warnings from the National Weather Service Bay Area .
 What About Atmospheric Rivers and El Niño?
 You may also hear terms like atmospheric river and El Niño in winter weather coverage. These describe weather and climate patterns, rather than specific levels of immediate danger.
 Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow regions of concentrated moisture in the atmosphere that can transport significant amounts of water vapor. When they move over land, they can produce substantial rainfall, particularly when storms linger or multiple systems arrive close together.
 Not every atmospheric river causes flooding. The impacts depend on factors including storm intensity, duration, soil conditions and how much rain has already fallen.
 El Niño is a climate pattern in the tropical Pacific Ocean that can influence seasonal weather patterns. While it may affect the likelihood of certain winter conditions, it does not guarantee that Sonoma will experience severe storms or flooding.
 Seasonal outlooks help us understand possibilities. As individual storms approach, local forecasts and alerts provide the information needed to make decisions.
 Weather Alerts vs. Emergency Notifications
 Weather forecasts and warnings are only part of staying informed.
 The National Weather Service provides information about expected weather conditions and hazards. Local public safety agencies may issue emergency notifications when specific protective actions are needed, such as evacuation warnings or orders.
 Not every storm will result in a local emergency notification. Residents should monitor weather forecasts when storms are expected rather than relying solely on emergency alerts.
 Before significant weather arrives:
 Check that you’re signed up for SoCo Alert and Nixle and that your contact information is current.
 Follow National Weather Service Bay Area for forecasts and weather alerts.
 Bookmark the City’s Emergency Updates page and SoCoEmergency.org for local emergency information.
 Know your evacuation zone and understand the difference between an evacuation warning and an evacuation order.
 Keep KSVY 91.3 FM in mind as a local source of information during emergencies.
 What Did Today’s Rain Tell You?
 Today’s rain is a useful reminder that winter readiness doesn’t always require a major project. Sometimes it starts with noticing something that needs attention.
 Before the next storm:
 Around your home: Check gutters, downspouts and drainage areas. Did water collect where it shouldn’t?
 Around your property: Clear leaves and debris and keep them out of streets and storm drains.
 On the road: Check your windshield wipers, headlights and tire condition. Allow extra travel time when roads are wet.
 If you’ve experienced flooding: Review your preparations and know where to find sandbags before you need them.
 Around your household: Check emergency supplies and backup charging options in case of a power outage.
 Never drive through flooded roadways or attempt to clear flooded drainage facilities.
 Prepare Now. Stay Informed. Be Ready.
 The City of Sonoma and its regional partners prepare for winter weather throughout the season, but household preparedness remains an important part of community readiness.
 We can’t know exactly what this winter will bring. We can use the information available, pay attention as forecasts change and take practical steps before conditions become hazardous.
 Visit Winter Ready Sonoma for seasonal preparedness information, sandbag resources, emergency contacts, weather updates and links to additional guidance from the City and Sonoma County.
